summary: No reviewer blocker survives verification as a blocker, but eleven should-fix defects do, so the spec is not approvable at rev 10. Two of the four headline blockers were checked directly against the tree and git: reviewer 5's "the gate rebase replays unaudited non-bundle commits" is wrong because §10.1.5 step 5 pushes local main to origin BEFORE recording main_pre_bootstrap, so at the gate origin/main..main equals the audited range (the 16-commit / 4-non-bundle drift is real, but the push carries it as ordinary main history); reviewer 4's "guaranteed" rebase failure is mechanically real (reproduced: git rebase refuses a dirty tracked file, exit 1) and lib/finish-step.mjs commits only at branch_finish resolution (:375) and archive (:404), but prior-run history (2fcbeab "state before merge") shows the shell committing before answering the gate, so it is reachable-not-guaranteed and loud, i.e. should-fix. The remaining reviewer blockers (publish-before-gates with no rollback; §7.3 strict tip equality vs state commits; this run's archive lacking a completion class) are genuine design gaps confirmed from the spec text but overstated in consequence: the "livelock" needs a commit on re-entry that the code never makes, the ordering is forced by G6 being a frozen goal so the defect is the missing failure disposition, and the missing completion class is undefined doctor behavior rather than data loss. Also confirmed in-tree: install-pi --check and plugin-registry-drift never execute the installed binary; ci.yml's release-publish job is gated on tests and G6 ignores it; main is unprotected with merge commits allowed (which drops reviewer 2's branch-protection scenario). Verdict: revise.
disagreements: Reviewer 5 (blocker: the gate rebase replays a strict superset of the audited range) vs reviewers 3 and 4 (§10 git mechanics sound): the evidence favours 3/4. §10.1.5 step 5 pushes local main to origin BEFORE recording main_pre_bootstrap, so after the GitHub merge merge-base(main, origin/main) == main_pre_bootstrap and `git rebase origin/main` replays exactly the audited commits. The drift reviewer 5 measured (16 ahead, 4 non-bundle) is real and is pushed in step 5 as ordinary main history, not replayed unaudited; retained only as a nit about the false 'behind by exactly those' sentence.

Reviewers 1 and 2 (blocker, 'livelock' on §7.3 strict tip equality) vs the tree: lib/finish-step.mjs commits the bundle only at branch_finish resolution (:375) and archive (:404); re-entry's deploy_base write is an uncommitted event, so the loop does not self-perpetuate. The inconsistency with §10.1.5 is real and the spurious re-entry / same-version re-certification is a should-fix, but 'can never reach run_final_check' is unsupported.

Reviewer 4 (blocker: rebase failure is 'guaranteed') vs in-tree history: the mechanism is confirmed (reproduced exit 1) and no commit site precedes the gate in finish-step, but the prior run's commits 2fcbeab ('finish adversary digest + state before merge') and 2bc21eb (branch_finish commit carrying only the branch_finish event) show the shell committing before answering the gate. Reachable-not-guaranteed, loud, recoverable → should-fix.

Reviewers 1 and 2 (blocker: publish before gates) vs reviewer 3 (should-fix; the 'merge normally, install later' alternative fails because G6 is a frozen goal of this run and the v9 goal check precedes branch_finish): reviewer 3's framing is right — the ordering is forced by the frozen goals, so the defect is the absent failure disposition after the first irreversible step, not the ordering itself.

Reviewer 2 (branch protection / squash-only could break `gh pr merge --merge`) vs reviewer 3 (verified unprotected): reviewer 3 is right — `gh api .../branches/main/protection` returns 404 and the repo allows merge commits — but reviewer 3's residual (the real gh pr create/merge cycle is never rehearsed and a transient failure has no disposition) stands and is merged into the first finding.

Reviewer 1 (blocker) vs reviewer 2 (nit) on this run's own archive lacking a completion class: should-fix — the doctor/runs-list behavior on the first bundle they inspect is genuinely unspecified, but nothing is lost and a one-paragraph bootstrap exception closes it.
dropped: Reviewer 5's blocker as stated (`git rebase origin/main` replays unaudited non-bundle commits): §10.1.5 step 5 pushes local main before recording main_pre_bootstrap, so at the gate origin/main..main == main_pre_bootstrap..main; the 4 non-bundle commits (abc3b0a, 5aa3c27, 0b6159d, af52fe8) are pushed as ordinary main history in step 5, not replayed by the rebase. The residual doc inaccuracy is kept as a nit.
Reviewer 2's should-fix on GitHub branch protection / required checks / squash-only breaking `gh pr merge --merge`: verified via `gh api` — main is unprotected (404) and allow_merge_commit is true.

Reviewer 2's blocker 'a failed final assessment has no terminal path': goals_unmet offers fix / waiver / abort (lib/finish-step.mjs:286-299, :518) and §7.2/§11 open intent_confirm after any final receipt, so waiver → intent_confirm → --intent-rejected → incomplete_authorized is reachable; downgraded to a nit about the dead 'fix' option and the unnamed route.
Reviewer 2's 'livelock' characterization of §7.3: requires a bundle commit on re-entry that the tree never makes; the underlying inconsistency is retained as a should-fix.
Reviewer 4's 'guaranteed dirty' qualifier: prior-run commit 2fcbeab shows the shell committing bundle state before the gate answer; the rebase-refusal mechanism itself is retained as a should-fix.
Reviewer 3's self-discarded 'merge normally and install as a follow-up' alternative: the reviewer withdrew it and the reason (G6 is a frozen goal checked before branch_finish) is correct.
Reviewer 1's separate 'same-version base-move re-certification' finding: valid but the same defect as the §7.3 state-only/code distinction and folded into that finding rather than counted twice.

findings.claim: §10 places every irreversible rollout step (release tag, tag push, install-pi, GitHub PR merge, Claude plugin update) before mp finish's verify / goal-check / adversary-review gates, and defines no disposition for a failure at any point after the first irreversible step — neither mid-wave (a failed or partial gh pr merge at step 5 after the tag push and Pi install at step 4, the one first-time live action the rehearsal cannot exercise) nor post-publish (a partial goal verdict or blocking review after both surfaces are live), while §10.1.3 freezes the branch tip so any fix commit breaks tag identity.
findings.failure: Step 4 pushes v10.0.0 and moves the Pi install root to v10; step 5's gh pr merge fails transiently (or step 2's goal check returns partial on G3) → v10 is live and tagged, the run cannot add a commit without violating 'tag == tip', goals_unmet offers only fix (foreclosed) / waiver / abort, and the spec names no corrective-release, downgrade, or incomplete-archive path; the run stalls with rejected code on both daily-driver surfaces.
findings.fix_direction: Keep the ordering (G6 forces it) but add a named failure disposition for each irreversible step: a corrective v10.0.x release path for post-publish gate failures, install-pi --ref=v9.10.0 rollback for the Pi surface, an explicit recovery state for a failed/partial PR merge, and either a throwaway-repo rehearsal of the real gh pr create/merge cycle or a documented residual-risk statement.
findings.location: docs/masterplan/intent-to-completion/spec.md §10 steps 1.3–1.6 (lines 531–560) vs step 2 (lines 566–585); §10.1.3 'From here the branch tip does not move'

findings.claim: §10.2's gate-time `git -C MAIN rebase origin/main` runs while MAIN's tracked bundle files (state.yml, events.jsonl) carry uncommitted writes from run_verify / goal check / retro / review / gate-open, and git rebase refuses a dirty tracked file; the spec's gate procedure lists no commit or --autostash before the rebase.
findings.failure: Reproduced: an unrelated uncommitted edit to a tracked file → `git rebase other` exits 1 with 'cannot rebase: You have unstaged changes' (merge fast-forwards fine, --autostash rebases fine). In-tree, lib/finish-step.mjs calls commitBundle only at branch_finish resolution (:375) and archive (:404); every earlier finish op writes via writeState/appendEvent (:232, :253, :271, :282, :370) without committing, and `mp event` (bin/masterplan.mjs:1037) appends only. Unless the shell commits first — which the spec does not require, though 2bc21eb/2fcbeab show it happened in a prior run — the gate step stops the walk with v10 already live.
findings.fix_direction: Make it normative in §10.2 that pending bundle state is committed (commitBundle-equivalent, bundle pathspec only) immediately before the audit and rebase, or use `git rebase --autostash origin/main`; require the rehearsal to drive the real op sequence through the pinned binary so the gate is reached with the same dirty state.

findings.claim: §7.3 requires MAIN's base tip to equal deploy_base_sha exactly at every later boundary, but §10.1.5 and the sequencer (commands/masterplan.md:96, :111) establish that bundle-state commits land on MAIN's base branch during finish (gate resolutions commit the bundle); the spec never says whether deploy-stage gates (deploy_failed, deploy_indeterminate, intent_confirm) commit, so any state-only commit between deploy_base and a later boundary trips 'base moved', discards the final receipt, and re-runs every check — and the check-only re-entry then re-certifies a same-version code commit without redeploying.
findings.failure: deploy_base recorded at A; step 1's deploy_failed gate is resolved 'retry' and the shell commits the bundle per the 'other gates → commit the bundle' convention → tip is S ≠ A → next run_deploy_step is 'dispatch-error: base moved'; re-entry records deploy_base at S and only re-runs `check`s, so if S (or any later main commit) were a same-version code change, tag-exists / install --check --expect=v10.0.0 still exit 0 and completion_confirmed binds to S while the live install is A's code. Not a livelock (re-entry's write is not a commit), but a spurious-re-entry defect on one side and a false re-certification on the other.
findings.fix_direction: Port §10.1.5's per-commit audit to §7.3: commits in deploy_base_sha..tip that touch only docs/masterplan/<slug>/ do not count as a base move; a commit touching anything else forces a full re-run of every step, not check-only. Add a finish-replay test with a real git repo and the real event writer.
findings.location: docs/masterplan/intent-to-completion/spec.md §7.3 (Dispositions and commit identity) vs §10.1.5 lines 540-546; commands/masterplan.md:96

findings.claim: This run archives under v9.10.0, which writes no state.completion, completion_confirmed, or incomplete_authorized, so under the v10 invariant of §7.4 its own archive has no completion class; §6.1 grants a bootstrap exception for goals.md but nothing grants one for completion, and the successor v10-validation run that alone proves the automated flow is left as a retro follow-up that §3 explicitly allows to remain open.
findings.failure: v10 ships; `runs list`, `mp status`, and the doctor's incomplete-archive check inspect the intent-to-completion bundle first and find an archived run with neither authorization event and no completion field — behavior unspecified (false INFO, crash, or silently 'complete'). G1–G6 read as met while Outcome 7's second sentence (successor exercises deploy-to-confirm) is never required to happen.
findings.fix_direction: Add a normative bootstrap exception parallel to §6.1: archives lacking the completion field classify as `legacy` (never complete) and the doctor reports them as such; and either make the v10-validation run a required (not deferrable) follow-up or make Outcome 7 explicitly conditional on its completion:complete archive.
findings.location: docs/masterplan/intent-to-completion/spec.md §7.4 (Completion class) vs §6.1 bootstrap exception and §3 'Deferred follow-ups in retros may remain open'

findings.claim: The interview floor is defined over answered questions but the `exhausted` exit at the cap requires only asked == cap and zero unanswered; withdrawn questions count against the cap and satisfy 'zero unanswered', so an interview can reach exhausted with zero operator answers.
findings.failure: complexity: high (floor 8, cap 20): ask 20 intent questions, withdraw all 20, record a draft built from the model's own assumptions → `mp interview end --reason=exhausted` validates (asked == cap, no unanswered, draft is latest content event) and goals-load accepts; Outcome 1's core defense never engages.
findings.fix_direction: Require floor met (answered ≥ floor) for every non-waived terminal state including exhausted-at-cap, or cap the number of withdrawn questions that may count toward the cap.

findings.claim: The `exhausted` exit and §5.1 step 5 carry forward only the `unknowns` of the latest critic payload; `contradictions` and `misclassified` from a prior successful payload are neither required to be resolved nor recorded, and a `critic_unavailable` after that payload makes exhausted immediately valid.
findings.failure: Critic round 1 returns unknowns: [] but contradictions: [C1]; the next dispatch times out → `critic --unavailable`; floor is met → exhausted validates with nothing to list; C1 is never written to the Assumptions table, never seen by the design phase or the final assessor, and is baked into frozen goals via a trigger the spec treats as ordinary.
findings.fix_direction: Define exhausted's recording obligation over the latest available payload's unknowns, contradictions, and misclassified entries, and require the assumed rows to cover all three; add the clean-unknowns/dirty-contradictions → unavailable → exhausted case to interview-ledger-resume.

findings.claim: `done:` is resolved once at `mp seed` and written into state.yml (§4.1), with no stated re-resolution at deploy-stage entry, so a branch that adds or changes the repo's `done:` block after seed has finish execute the stale seed-time definition — and this very run adds `.masterplan.yaml` on its branch (§12 lists it as New).
findings.failure: Seed records done: absent (or version_from/steps X); the branch commits a `.masterplan.yaml` declaring the real definition; after merge, finish reads state.yml and opens no_definition_of_done (or runs X) while the merged repo's actual declaration never executes; checks pass and the run archives complete.
findings.fix_direction: Re-resolve `done:` from `<MAIN>/.masterplan.yaml` at deploy_base_sha on deploy-stage entry (seed-time validation stays as an early check); add config tests that change/add/remove done: on the branch after seed and assert which definition runs.
findings.location: docs/masterplan/intent-to-completion/spec.md §4.1 ('done ... repo-local only', 'mp seed ... writes the resolved values into state.yml') vs §7.2 no_definition_of_done row; §12 New: `.masterplan.yaml`

findings.claim: §4.4's knob-contract guard accepts 'a seeded state field' as the observable difference between two knob values, which is writer-only proof and would pass exactly the inert --complexity/--autonomy defect class this change exists to close.
findings.failure: Add --region, store it in state.yml, read it nowhere; register a contract test seeding --region=us vs --region=eu and asserting the two state fields differ → knob-inventory and knob-contract both pass on a completely inert knob.
findings.fix_direction: Drop 'a seeded state field' from the accepted observables; require an mp op, gate, event, or rendered protocol line to differ, and make the synthetic read-but-ignored fixture include the seeded-field-only case as a guard-must-fail example.

findings.claim: The mandatory live_check group and G6's evidence set verify only structural install state; neither real implementation they call ever executes the installed masterplan binary, so a structurally valid but functionally broken install satisfies every check.
findings.failure: bin/install-pi.mjs:205-248 check() verifies the `current` symlink, .pi-install.json sha, validateSnapshot (REQUIRED_PATHS existence only, :90-93), skill-link targets, and agent-registration text drift; lib/doctor/plugin-registry-drift.mjs:57-80 diffs installed_plugins.json version/sha against the marketplace plugin.json. A packaging bug visible only under releases/<sha>/ (e.g. a file git-archive drops) yields check_ok on Pi and version-match on Claude, G6 reads met, live_check passes, the run archives complete, and the next /masterplan on the Pi surface crashes. (Mitigation already present: §10.1.6 does run the Claude-cache binary's `version` as shell-verified evidence, but G6's frozen evidence list and the Pi surface have no execution probe.)
findings.fix_direction: Add one behavior-exercising step to live_check and to G6's evidence: invoke the installed binary on each surface (`node <install-root>/current/bin/masterplan.mjs version` / doctor through the installed copy) with an exit-code check.
findings.location: docs/masterplan/intent-to-completion/spec.md:314-328 (done block), :339 (mandatory groups), :561 (G6 evidence); goals.md G6 evidence; bin/install-pi.mjs:205-248; lib/doctor/plugin-registry-drift.mjs:57-80

findings.claim: Pushing the v10.0.0 tag (§10 step 4) triggers .github/workflows/ci.yml's `test` job and, `needs: test`, the `release-publish` job that creates the GitHub Release; G6's evidence (tag exists locally and remotely, install-pi --check, plugin-registry-drift) never queries that run, so a red CI on the tagged commit leaves G6 reading met.
findings.failure: Tag push fires ci.yml; the unit suite or doctor fails on the tagged commit (or the CHANGELOG-section extraction fails, which the workflow treats as a hard error); the tag still exists on origin, no Release is created, and every G6 command still exits 0.
findings.fix_direction: Add a G6 / release-group check that queries the tag's workflow run (`gh run list --branch v10.0.0` or the Actions API) and treats a failed or still-pending release-publish as deploy_failed / deploy_indeterminate.

findings.claim: By the time the pinned v9.10.0 finish dispatches the goal assessor and adversary review, both agent surfaces are already on v10 (plugin cache reloaded at step 6, Pi agents re-registered by install-pi at step 4), so the v2 mp-goal-assessor / adversary prompts are invoked in a v9 single-dispatch shape against a v1 goals.md, and no compatibility is asserted or rehearsed.
findings.failure: The v2 assessor prompt expects an Intent block and an intent_verdict field in its final mode; handed a v1 goals.md by the v9 dispatch it may emit a malformed or wrong verdict that v9's record-goal-check accepts; the rehearsal only asserts a non-empty diff reached the assessor.
findings.fix_direction: State the compatibility contract (v2 prompts must accept a v1 goals.md and the v9 dispatch shape) and add a test or rehearsal assertion for it, or pin the agent prompt version used by this run's finish independently of the installed surface.

findings.claim: The sample done: block's install-group check `git ls-remote --exit-code --tags origin refs/tags/v${version}` exits 2 (not 1) when the tag is absent, so §7.2's exit-status mapping classifies a deterministic 'absent' as deploy_indeterminate.
findings.failure: Reproduced against an empty bare remote: missing tag → exit 2; present tag → exit 0. Under the spec's mapping (0 present / 1 absent / other indeterminate) the absent case opens deploy_indeterminate offering 'mark done with evidence' instead of deploy_failed.
findings.fix_direction: Wrap the sample as `... || exit 1` (or treat documented not-found codes as absent), and test the literal sample against a tagless remote.
findings.location: docs/masterplan/intent-to-completion/spec.md §7.1 sample check line and §7.2 exit-status contract

findings.claim: §10.1.5 asserts GitHub main is behind local main 'by exactly' this bundle's state commits; in-tree local main is 16 commits ahead of origin/main and 4 of them (abc3b0a, 5aa3c27 policy/workflow-map.json; 0b6159d, af52fe8 WORKLOG.md) are non-bundle, and the rehearsal's scratch clone starts in sync so this never gets modeled.
findings.failure: Step 5's `git push origin main` carries unrelated commits to GitHub — harmless to the gate (the push precedes main_pre_bootstrap, so the rebase and audit ranges coincide), but the sentence is false and a WORKLOG.md overlap between those commits and the PR branch would surface as a PR-merge conflict the spec does not anticipate.
findings.fix_direction: Correct the sentence to 'local main may be ahead by unrelated commits; the push carries them and main_pre_bootstrap is recorded after it', and start the rehearsal fixture from a clone already ahead of its remote.

findings.claim: After the final assessment, the goals_unmet gate's `fix` option is dead (worktree gone), and the spec does not name the route to an incomplete archive from a missed final verdict, though one exists (waiver → intent_confirm → --intent-rejected).
findings.failure: Operator picks 'fix' on a post-live goals_unmet; finish stops with reason goals_unmet_fix (lib/finish-step.mjs:299) and there is nothing to fix in; the operator has to discover the waiver → reject route unaided.
findings.fix_direction: State in §6.2/§7.2 that the final goals_unmet offers waiver / abort / reject-intent only, with reject writing incomplete_authorized directly.

findings.claim: High complexity's 'critic after every intent round' (§4.2) is not enforceable: the ledger has no round-boundary event, and §5.4 converged validates only the latest receipt.
findings.failure: Eight intent questions across several rounds with no critic between them, one draft, one clean critic, one design pick → converged passes every §5.4 condition; after compaction the ledger cannot show rounds were skipped.
findings.fix_direction: Either record a round-boundary event (per AskUserQuestion call) and validate a critic receipt after each at high, or document the per-round rule as advisory.

findings.claim: run_deploy_step executes from MAIN's live working tree (`cwd: MAIN`) while receipts bind only to the branch-ref sha; an uncommitted local edit to a tracked script (release.mjs, install-pi.mjs, .masterplan.yaml) runs unrecorded.
findings.failure: Tip == deploy_base_sha; scripts/release.mjs has a local uncommitted modification; the step runs the modified file, its check passes, and the receipt attributes the effect to the committed sha.
findings.fix_direction: Run deploy steps from a clean detached checkout of deploy_base_sha, or fail closed when `git status --porcelain` shows non-bundle changes.

findings.claim: The seed-time overlap check is a TOCTOU between `mp runs list` and `mp seed`, and the overlap_review event proves only that a JSON file was appended, not which inventory snapshot it considered.
findings.failure: Two concurrent seeds each see no conflicting run and both record empty candidate lists; a stale review file likewise passes.
findings.fix_direction: Bind overlap_review to a digest of the runs-list snapshot it was computed from; add a concurrent-seed test.
